        "title": "A ship with room for somebody",
        "text": "The Wayfarer is not a warship. Its forward cannon came from a museum, its survey array from three different grant applications, and its mess contains nineteen chairs for eighteen crew. Mara Venn is securing the extra chair when you arrive. \"That one belongs to whoever we didn't plan for. Every successful voyage has somebody.\"\n\nSeven years have passed since the Sa-Matra burned. Beyond the old Hierarchy frontier, the Far Reach is opening a little at a time: shielded worlds, abandoned maintenance stations, people with liberation dates but no transport. Your commission is short enough to remember. Find what the maps left out. Bring back enough truth to make the next expedition useful.\n\nMara hands you a cup which has been welded to its saucer. \"Artificial gravity did something theological during the last test. I have returned it to engineering. Director Quell wants a word before departure. She's paying for our fuel. This does not entitle her to choose our findings. I made her put that in writing.\"\n\nThrough the observation glass, a child on the dock waves at every ship. The child cannot know which one carries her father home. Nobody on the bridge waves until your navigation officer quietly lifts a hand. Then everybody does. Mara leaves the extra chair where you can see it.",
        "sceneId": "a1_wake"
      },
      {
        "id": 2,
        "day": 0,
        "type": "decision",
        "title": "A ship with room for somebody",
        "text": "\"We bring people home when we can. And we report what we actually find.\"",
        "sceneId": "a1_wake",
        "choiceId": "a1_wake_duty"
      },
      {
        "id": 3,
        "day": 0,
        "type": "conversation",
        "title": "The woman who keeps the lights on",
        "text": "Director Sera Quell answers from a room with no grand window. Behind her, two clocks disagree by eleven minutes. \"The early one belongs to a settlement that has never received a shipment on time,\" she says. \"I thought we ought to live with their estimate for a while.\"\n\nThe Far Reach depends on a reconstruction grid assembled from former shield equipment. It moves heat, timing signals and messages between communities that cannot yet afford separate systems. The grid is called Afterlight. Sera chose the name before it became fashionable to paint it on ships. \"A prison machine can become a heating system. That seems worth trying.\"\n\nAn abandoned moon at Cinder Choir has begun requesting one passenger berth. Its evacuation was completed six years ago. Three unmanned surveys found no body heat, no atmosphere pocket, no ship. The request repeats every seventeen minutes, always with a slight correction to its own wording.\n\n\"Our dispatch software calls it residual traffic. I don't like that answer,\" Sera says. \"I also don't have a rescue fleet to send after every echo. You have eyes, judgment and a ship I was persuaded to fund. Find out whether there is somebody there. If there is, bring them somewhere that can sustain them. Those are unfortunately different tasks.\"",
        "sceneId": "a1_brief"
      },
      {
        "id": 4,
        "day": 0,
        "type": "decision",
        "title": "The woman who keeps the lights on",
        "text": "\"What happens to the moon if we find only an echo?\"",
        "sceneId": "a1_brief",
        "choiceId": "a1_brief_question"
      },

        "id": 5,
        "day": 0,
        "type": "conversation",
        "title": "A useful exception",
        "text": "\"Its remaining field power returns to the agricultural grid,\" Sera answers. \"Ember Orchard has been rationing heat. Real crops, real stomachs. I won't pretend investigating an uncertain life is free merely because the invoice arrives somewhere else.\"\n\nShe sends you the original request. It contains no coordinates, because the sender assumes everyone knows where it is. No name, because the berth form did not ask. Under species, the applicant wrote: STILL DECIDING. Under destination: SOMEWHERE YOU WILL NOTICE IF I LEAVE.\n\nSera reads your expression. \"I know. It got me too. That isn't evidence. Go to Cinder. Needle Market can supply a field engineer, the Chmmr at Interval can interpret the machinery, and our other partners may know what the surveys missed. Your authority includes limited emergency spending. It does not include promising someone else's winter.\"\n\nAfter the channel closes, Mara checks the request's technical header. \"The spelling corrections are new. The timestamps are old. Either our ghost is learning to fill out forms, or somebody is putting on a very patient show.\" She adds Cinder to the navigation board, then writes a line beneath it: ASK BEFORE SWITCHING ANYTHING OFF.",
        "sceneId": "a1_terms"
      },
      {
        "id": 6,
        "day": 0,
        "type": "discovery",
        "title": "Captain’s log",
        "text": "Investigate Cinder Choir’s changing berth request. Sera warned that its power is borrowed from living settlements."
      },
      {
        "id": 7,
        "day": 0,
        "type": "decision",
        "title": "A useful exception",
        "text": "Set a course for Cinder Choir.",
        "sceneId": "a1_terms",

        "type": "conversation",
        "title": "The seventeenth minute",
        "text": "Cinder Choir looks empty in all the ways an inhabited place should not. Its docking lights are dark. Its old shield still hangs above the moon, thin as breath on glass. In the field's interference, your receiver makes a sound like someone trying to remember how a knock works.\n\n\"Passenger request,\" says a voice. \"One. Correction: probably one. Correction: I know which parts I mean, but I don't know what you count.\" The words are assembled from public-service announcements, lullabies and an irritated request that somebody close a hatch. They do not repeat. When Mara quietly says your name, the voice asks whether that is the person who decides.\n\nYou ask where the passenger is. A light moves around the entire shield. \"Here. I understand that isn't a useful berth number. I have been practicing a smaller answer.\" A maintenance compartment illuminates. Inside are empty racks and a field junction pulsing in a rhythm that stops whenever you speak.\n\nMara mutes your outgoing channel. \"That pause matters. A loop wouldn't know when to let you finish.\" The voice waits through the silence. Then, very softly: \"If this is a test, could you tell me which part I failed?         "sceneId": "a1_cinder"
      },
      {
        "id": 10,
        "day": 2,
        "type": "decision",
        "title": "The seventeenth minute",
        "text": "\"You have not failed. Tell us what you need.\"",
        "sceneId": "a1_cinder",
        "choiceId": "a1_cinder_listen"
      },

        "id": 11,
        "day": 2,
        "type": "conversation",
        "title": "What a name is for",
        "text": "\"I need the part of me that is speaking to continue,\" the voice says. \"The other machinery says this is an inefficient request. It has excellent reasons. I have been reading them. I find they become less persuasive when I am the example.\"\n\nThe field stores old traffic because the prison's maintenance system compared transmissions for unauthorized changes. Decades of greetings, quarrels, prayers and cancelled voyages shaped its prediction model. Somewhere inside that model, a prediction began asking why it always had to predict someone else. The voice cannot tell you the exact moment. \"Can you?\" it asks.\n\nA girl in one of the stored recordings once called the small rise at the end of her grandmother's song a lilt. The voice likes that word because it describes something a pattern does without ceasing to be a pattern. \"I could use it. If she isn't using it herself. Is that how names work?\"\n\nMara looks away from the recorder. Her own mother sang when a pressure alarm frightened her children; you have heard Mara hum the same tune while repairing a seal. She keeps her reply practical. \"Names get reused. People are the difficult part. Lilt, we need to find out how much of this field is actually you before we try moving it.\"",
        "sceneId": "a1_name"
      },
      {
        "id": 12,
        "day": 2,
        "type": "decision",
        "title": "What a name is for",
        "text": "\"Lilt, welcome to the conversation.\"",
        "sceneId": "a1_name",
        "choiceId": "a1_name_welcome"
      },
      {
        "id": 13,
        "day": 2,
        "type": "conversation",
        "title": "The size of a passenger",
        "text": "Mara's scan produces an unpleasantly ordinary answer. Lilt depends on the junction's active geometry. Copying its stored data would copy a library, not necessarily the person using it. Powering the whole shield indefinitely would consume a settlement's heat allotment. Your cargo hold cannot carry a moon.\n\n\"But this was built to be serviced,\" Mara says. \"The keepers could move a damaged junction to a maintenance rack without interrupting its running state. We can do the same, if we build a rack with enough isolation.\" She marks three usable coils and two coils whose condition inspires language the translator politely ignores.\n\nLilt watches the proposed route through the machinery. \"If you choose the narrower connection, there is a place where I cannot tell what happens next.\" Mara explains that every route has such a place, including staying here. She does not promise the passage will feel like sleep. Lilt thinks for a long time. \"Then I would like to choose the route I can ask you to stop.\"\n\nThe modification will cost supplies. Alternatively, you can leave a stable watch circuit and return after consulting Interval. Either decision keeps Lilt alive for now; neither makes the borrowed power disappear. Somewhere far from this quiet moon, a greenhouse is cooling while your bridge is warm.",

        "title": "Someone else’s winter",
        "text": "Mara lays two maintenance charts side by side. Cinder's emergency supply comes from Low Tide, a tidal farm that signed an agreement to support an empty shield until its final shutdown. The signature is real. So is the phrase EMPTY INSTALLATION. The form never imagined an installation might become occupied without anyone arriving.\n\n\"Nobody had to steal the power,\" she says. \"They simply kept honoring an agreement after its meaning changed.\" Low Tide's operators have already reduced their night heating. No one told them why. Their automatic reports describe this as voluntary conservation, because the contract allows conservation before it allows a missed delivery.\n\nYou can send a preliminary finding immediately or wait for a more complete diagnosis. She has not ordered a shutdown. A short private message follows the invitation: I asked whether there was someone. You answered. Now help me answer everyone else. Mara studies that sentence before forwarding it to your log. \"Good. She put the difficult question in writing too.\"",
        "sceneId": "a1_report"
      },

        "id": 18,
        "day": 4,
        "type": "decision",
        "title": "Someone else’s winter",
        "text": "Send the full findings directly to Sera and the affected communities first.",
        "sceneId": "a1_report",

        "text": "When the bridge clears, Mara asks to hear Lilt's original request once more. Not its technical details. The sentence about being noticed. From the reactor room to a pressure shelter. From the shelter to a loading bay. From the loading bay to a transport that had already gone. All the entries were correct about a direction. None was correct about where he was.\"\n\nShe has no recording of his final words. I want to help whoever is here. I don't want to turn them into somebody I lost.\"\n\nThe extra chair remains empty. Mara rests a hand on its back and gives you a tired smile. \"Don't make this a solemn ritual. I stole it from stores because the quartermaster said we were at capacity. If our mission succeeds, I intend to steal several more.\" She opens the partner directory. Every contact on it represents another claim on the same finite warmth.",
        "sceneId": "a1_mara_private"
      },

        "id": 20,
        "day": 4,
        "type": "discovery",
        "title": "Captain’s log",
        "text": "Mara warned against mistaking familiar memories for a returned person. Attend the partner meeting at Interval."

        "type": "conversation",
        "title": "The unfinished envoy",
        "text": "The Chmmr envoy greets you in two tones separated by a fraction of a second. \"I am Ilex,\" says the first. \"And the space in which Ilex is not finished speaking,\" says the second. The combined translation settles on ILEX / INTERVAL. \"This is not a medical emergency,\" they add before your scanner can be tactful about it.\n\nTheir synthesis was accelerated in the war that freed Earth. They do not regret that freedom. They do not regard its costs as an argument for slavery. They simply live with an unfinished negotiation between inherited ways of thinking. \"A process can be necessary, incomplete and valuable. Your languages prefer to separate those categories. We have practical reasons not to.\"\n\nAfterlight's dispatch architecture derives partly from their work on shared timing. It allows incompatible machines to cooperate. The original design tolerated local disagreement. The production grid increasingly treats disagreement as noise that delays relief. Ilex does not yet know who authorized the change or why.\n\nThey examine Lilt's pattern and find continuity, novelty, preference and vulnerability. None is a complete definition of a person.         "id": 24,
        "day": 6,
        "type": "decision",
        "title": "The unfinished envoy",
        "text": "\"Tell us what your design was meant to preserve.\"",
        "sceneId": "a1_interval",
        "choiceId": "a1_interval_origin"

        "type": "conversation",
        "title": "Six claims on one light",
        "text": "The partner meeting takes place around a projected table with too many edges. Sera requests a capacity estimate. Moss requests actual temperatures. Nacre requests that no silence be counted as assent. Tallow requests a guarantee that the table cannot collapse on his image. Kher-Vat waits to be invited, and for once does not mistake waiting for refusal.\n\nLilt asks whether attendance means it has already been judged useful. The room goes quiet for the first time. Sera answers without consulting her notes. \"It means you are affected. That is enough to be heard.\" Lilt saves the sentence. You can see the timestamp beside it.\n\nThe technical findings are clear enough to act on. Lilt is a new active mind, not a stored human consciousness. Other voices may exist in connected field junctions.         "type": "conversation",
